briefing.headline: Datadog dropped a brand-new PMM req and Figma's 'Audience & Messaging' role is your resume in a job posting — both are fresher and better matched than anything you've been shown all week.
briefing.focus: Spend today on the two net-new PMM reqs (Datadog Incident Response, posted yesterday; Figma Audience & Messaging) — both are big, established H-1B sponsors and both are IC-level, not senior. Then force a decision on the three roles you've now seen 5 times: CarGurus B2B Marketing Specialist (your only Boston B2B marketing role), the AWS IDC marketing-analytics BA, and Twilio's remote Marketing Analyst — apply or delete them today. Skip every Amazon posting with an 'AMZ#####' job number; those are PERM labor-certification notices, not real external openings.

ranked.why: Posted yesterday, zero prior pushes, IC-level PMM at a top-tier H-1B sponsor — apply before the pile builds.
'Audience & Messaging' is literally segmentation + positioning — the keyword score undersold this at 88; Figma is large enough to sponsor and lists US-wide.
The only Boston B2B marketing role at your exact level, at a public company — 5 pushes in, this is apply-today-or-delete.
Datadog PMM with no skill gaps; the containers/AI depth is a real stretch but the fintech-to-infra story is tellable.
The single best bridge of both lanes — marketing demand-gen analytics, SQL, dashboards — but Seattle-only and you've passed 5 times; decide.
Remote-US marketing analyst with funnel/attribution ownership at a known sponsor — the ideal shape; 5 pushes means commit or cut.
Stripe + payments = your banking/fintech domain is an asset here, not a translation problem; US-wide posting.
Partner marketing is ABM + enablement + co-branded collateral — your exact toolkit; ATS score of 64 badly under-rates the fit.
Fresh IC PMM at a 2,000+ person company with real momentum; San Mateo relocation is the only real cost.
Boston-based AWS PMM — rare combination of your city and a guaranteed sponsor; 5 pushes and still open says it's hard, not gone.
Amazon Business is genuine B2B PMM inside Amazon — closest thing to your current job at a company that sponsors at scale.
Core-product PMM at a company with strong brand pull; expect this to want more consumer/PLG instinct than you have.
Posted today at Anthropic — apply on freshness alone, but the bar and applicant volume here are brutal.
Third Datadog PMM opening — apply to two, not all four, and pick the ones where the product story is learnable.
Capital is SMB lending — your banking background is the differentiator, and it's remote-US at a top sponsor; the keyword score missed the domain match entirely.
Clean analyst-lane req at Amazon with no missing skills and only one prior push.
Boston, specialist level, public company — brand-side rather than demand-gen, but geography wins here.
Boston + Klaviyo + Salesforce/GTM systems ownership; it's more systems than marketing, which is why it keeps not converting.
ABM is the first line of your resume and this is a non-Sr ABM req at AWS — 4 pushes in, Arlington relocation is likely what's stopping you.
Remote-US GTM analytics with SQL at the center — perfect lane, but Lattice is mid-size and sponsorship is less certain than the big names.
Standard Amazon BA req, no gaps — a real opening (unlike the AMZ-numbered ones) and the safest sponsorship path in the analyst lane.
Partner/ISV marketing at AWS maps to your enablement and collateral work; only Marketo is missing.
Solid Datadog PMM but APM/profiler is the most technical of their four openings — lowest odds of the set.
Never pushed before and no skill gaps — a fresh analyst-lane shot, though grocery merch analytics is far from marketing.
Remote-US at a known sponsor and events is a real demand-gen channel; narrower than your background deserves.
Associate PMM is the one title in this list explicitly below your level — the 69 fit score is wrong about what matters, which is that you'd clear the bar easily.
Remote-US, specialist level, large sponsor — lifecycle/email is a narrower lane than PMM but a legitimate entry point.
US-remote GTM planning at Stripe with fintech domain fit; program management pulls away from marketing craft.
Associate-level and paid-LinkedIn focused — right level, but 4 straight pushes with no action means you've already judged it too narrow.
Legitimate sales-ops analyst work at a well-funded company, but no Boston/remote option and 3 prior pushes.
Fresh Amazon BA req; internal-workforce analytics is the least marketing-adjacent of the BA openings.
Full-marks keyword score on a vague 'Growth Marketing' title with no level stated — worth a look but the score is doing the talking, not the JD.
Genuinely interesting growth role, but Vercel is small, hybrid-only in three cities, and the agent-stack audience is deeply technical.
Promotions analytics is real marketing analytics, but Austin-only and 4 pushes without action.
Boston analyst role at a mid-size local employer — 5 pushes in, and SimpliSafe's sponsorship track record is thinner than the big tech names.
Associate-level GTM strategy at a strong sponsor; ops-heavy and one of four near-identical Datadog GTM reqs.
Field marketing at Anthropic is legitimate lane fit, but SF/NYC only and the competition is severe.
Scored 100 on keywords but it's health-insurance sales ops — licensing-adjacent, no marketing content, and 4 pushes ignored.
